newsitem.title: BRAZIL: EU trade envoy holds talks in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: EU trade envoy holds talks in Brazil.

text.p: A European Union trade envoy held talks with Brazilian officials on Thursday, touching on a wide range of subjects ahead of December's first summit of the World Trade Organization (WTO), officials said.

Jose Alfredo Graca Lima, head of the Brazilian Foreign Ministry's Economics Department, said envoy Jean-Pierre Leng met Foreign Minister Luiz Felipe Lampreia and Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles.
"We agree on most issues," Graca Lima told reporters. "There are few areas with great clashes of interest."
EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan recently appointed Leng special trade envoy to Brazil, according to a Foreign Ministry statement issued earlier on Thursday.

"This visit signals the growing importance with which the EU regards cooperation with Brazil and the need to exert all efforts to ensure full success at the ministerial meeting in Singapore," it said.
Graca Lima said talks with Leng centered on key issues to be dealth with in Singapore.
He said the EU position on the controversial "social clause", which would tie workers' rights to the question of trade and is fervently opposed by Brazil, was slightly vague.

"Leng explained that the community was in favour of a practical solution, not confrontation," Graca Lima said, adding that he speculated this could mean coming up with a formulation on workers' rights that did not tie them to trade issues.

The December WTO summit will be the first since the organization came into being after the Uruguay round of trade talks and is intended to review progress so far towards global free trade and to map the way ahead.
